lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. No decision is needed from Brandon now.

The tenth publish went live at 21:49 UTC (2:49 PM MT) and I took it back at 21:56 UTC (2:56 PM MT). The live page is the ninth publish's build again. Why: a minute after the publish the controls builder reported that on chain 38's tree summer cannot be made at quality low and at quality medium. One guard in summer's village, new in chain 38, expects the full list of the lawn's corners and stops the making when the page draws a lighter list; the page then never shows summer and gives no controls (stated by the builder, who read it in a browser; the code line read by me; git says the line is in chain 38 and not in the ninth publish). At high, and at the plain address on the helper machine, summer comes. So a phone or a tablet that draws below high would have lost summer. Nothing I ran could see it: the capture page reads the full set, and my live checks read the page only at the quality it picks for itself. That gap is mine and is closed from now on: every live check and the measuring run read all four seasons at low and medium as well.

The page was back on the ninth's build 7 minutes and 37 seconds after the tenth went live. The ninth's tree was built again here: its 17 checked files are equal by sha256 to the ones the ninth publish's security reviewer listed, and the folder has the same 327 files and 160,423,773 bytes as on the ninth. Not known yet: whether the ninth's own tree draws all four seasons at low and medium, since it was never read there either. A helper reads that now, and reads the fault on the tenth's tree with a second pair of eyes.

The mend is three lines, proposed by the controls builder and being proven on its machine. It goes in as one commit of its own with a test that would have caught it, then into main, then the eleventh publish.

The change of season was judged by a fresh critic on chain 38's strips at preview size: 8 of 10, ready to film: yes. It calls three of the four changes clean and names fall into winter as the one a viewer could catch: the table goes cold blue a few frames before the core is white. I read its items against the kit before they went on. That item is struck: the kit says the room light crosses across the window and the outside things change inside a bloom of the new season's light, and on the strip the blue on the table rises together with the white in the globe. One nudge went to the change's builder: at summer into fall the sand base's coloured glass dots still show while the twig base climbs. It answered at 22:00 UTC that this will not be whole by the close, so it stays as it is. It also says its second item, the grainy fringe on the arriving petals at film frame 680, is not bettered by the line it built (2.57 levels before, 2.46 after, by its measure), so it holds that line back and pushes only its first item, the pale patch at frames 669 to 671, which is gone.

Winter's critic: 8 of 10, not ready to film. The storm at the landing is a tight ring and the miniature stays readable, against the settled line that more than half of the miniature is hidden; the tree is dark under bright bulbs; the pond is flat grey; the lamp blows out. Winter has no builder in round two; its list goes into the question to Brandon as it stands.
So all five critics of round two are in: summer 5, fall 5, spring 6, winter 8, the change of season 8. None of the four seasons is called ready to film. His eye outranks their scores and mine.

A fault in the film that the critic did not name and I see on the same strip: at film frames 1388 and 1389 the table's petals leave as rows of copies, like comb teeth (open item 268). The shutter's builder drew frame 1388 at 3840 at the masters' tier (76 samples, 741 seconds, stated by it): the rib is finer there, copies 8 to 14 pixels apart, and still readable at the petals' edges at full size (a cut is attached). Its mend is ordered: the petals drawn as streaks, the way the sand and the lights already are. Its builder guesses the cost at under 5 percent of those frames' drawing time; not measured.

Fall's air: its builder measured that the dark night air the critic asked for is nearer the approved picture than main's pale wash, and that it takes the miniature's part of one measuring number from 0.975 to 0.909, below a floor of 0.974 I had set. I ruled for the approved picture and lifted the floor to 0.90 for this push (decision 219).

The close of round two stays 22:50 UTC (3:50 PM MT). After it: the merges, one measuring run of everything together (chain 39) which now also reads low and medium, the eleventh publish, Preview 07, then the status that gives the live address with stills, says where each season stands and asks whether to move on to the film and the 4K masters. No round three without his word.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger, 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 06.
